About this document

This document provides the teaching content for Accounting Years 11–13 of the
New Zealand Curriculum.

Progress and assessment information for Accounting Years 11–13 is still in
development. Once that is completed, Accounting Years 11–13 is proposed to be
made by the Minister of Education as a National Curriculum Statement under section
90(1)(a) of the Education and Training Act 2020.

It is proposed that, once made and published in the New Zealand Gazette, schools
who offer Accounting Years 11–13 will be required to start using it in Year 11 from 1
January 2028, in Year 12 from 1 January 2029, and in Year 13 from 1 January 2030.

This document will be replaced with the official version made under the Act and
published in the New Zealand Gazette once that has occurred.

  In Accounting, students are taught how financial and non-financial information is
  used to support decision-making in business and organisational contexts.
  Students are taught how to interpret, apply, and communicate accounting
  information using relevant concepts and practices, such as analysing financial
  performance and position to inform planning and improvement.

Students are taught core accounting principles and how to organise financial
information. Students explain why accounting systems, conventions, and
internationally recognised practices are important for business success.

Accounting provides students with the knowledge and practices to examine trends in
reports and respond to real-world and theoretical contexts, including interpreting basic
financial statements. This disciplinary knowledge helps students to develop expertise
in analysing and preparing financial statements by learning correct layout, heading,
and accounting vocabulary.

As students progress through Accounting Years 11–13, they are taught to interpret,
analyse, and draw conclusions from financial and non-financial information to make
justified decisions in written form. This enables them to make recommendations that
are strategic, evidence-based, and grounded in a broader understanding of business
context, ethics, and long-term implications.

  Accounting leads to pathways in accounting and related fields, such as
  commerce, finance, and economics.
